evidence: The use of TiON films by plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition as insulators in thin film electroluminescent ~TFEL! devices was examined and compared with that of TiO2 by ALD. A ZnS:Mn TFEL device using AlON-TiON stacked insulator ~ATON! exhibited the figure of merit of 12 mC/cm2. The luminance of the TFEL device with an ATON insulator was twice as high as that with a conventional Al2O3 insulator. This high performance can be attributed not only to high dielectric constant of the ATON film, but the improved quality of the interface of the phosphor and insulator, as well. In the TiO2-ALD and TiON-PEALD processes, titanium isopropoxide ~TTIP! was used as the Ti precursor and H2O served as the O precursor in the ALD, and O2 and N2 were the O and N precursors in the PEALD process, respectively. Trimethyl aluminum ~TMA! was used as the Al precursor and O2 and N2 were used as O and N precursors in the AlON-PEALD process. A PEALD apparatus using radio-frequency plasma was manufactured by Genitech. The AlON and TiO2 or TiON films can be deposited consecutively in the reactor and the deposition temperature and working pressure were fixed at 250°C and 3 torr, respectively. The RF plasma power was 300 W and plasma was turned on only during the supply of the O2 and N2 reactant gas. To compare the breakdown strength of AlON-TiO2 ~ATO! and that of AlON-TiON ~ATON!, samples with a simple structure of Al/insulator/ITO/Glass were prepared. Table I shows the breakdown fields and leakage current at 2 MV/cm for the ATO and ATON films deposited on ITO/Glass with various thickness ratios of AlON to TiON and AlON to TiO2. As shown in Table I, the breakdown fields for the ATON samples are higher than those of the ATO samples. In the case where the thickness ratio of AlON to TiON is 3, the breakdown strength of ATON film is 8.5 MV/cm which corresponds to or exceeds the best data for an Al2O3 grown by ALE. From the slope at the high field of the charge density-voltage ~Q-V! curve, the values of the dielectric constant of the insulating layer were estimated. Dielectric constant of ATON films~1:1! can be obtained from the dielectric constant of the ATON insulators of the top insulator and the AlON layer of the bottom insulator, and as a result, a relative dielectric constant of about 21 was obtained. The L40 of the sample with TiON/AlON ~1:1! is about twice as high as that of the standard sample, where L40 is defined as the luminance at 40 V above the threshold voltage. Figure 3 shows the luminous efficiency vs. modulation voltage characteristics of the five samples, where an arbitrary unit is used for representing the luminous efficiency and where the modulation voltage indicates the volts above the threshold voltage. Clamping voltages of the active layer were estimated from Q-V curves. Clamping voltages of 107 and 87 V were obtained for the sample with TiON/AlON ~1:1! and the sample with ALD-TiO2 /AlON ~1:3!, respectively. In summary, ATON films grown by PEALD provide, not only a stable TiON-ZnS interface which helps to improve the luminance of TFEL devices but also a layered structure with both a moderately high dielectric constant and a high breakdown field.
